47.english_meaning: The demand for money held in cash in anticipation of future changes in interest rates and bond prices.
47.hindi_meaning: सट्टेबाजी के उद्देश्य से मुद्रा की मांग (भविष्य में ब्याज दरों और बॉन्ड की कीमतों में बदलाव की उम्मीद में नकद रखने की इच्छा)
47.example: Speculative demand for money rises when investors expect bond prices to fall.

47.hindi_meaning: पूंजीगत हानि (किसी संपत्ति या बॉन्ड का मूल्य गिरने पर होने वाला घाटा)
47.example: An unexpected rise in interest rates can lead to capital losses for bondholders.

47.english_meaning: Responsive or sensitive to changes in economic variables such as price or interest rates.
47.hindi_meaning: लोचदार (आर्थिक चरों जैसे मूल्य या ब्याज दर में बदलाव के प्रति संवेदनशील)

47.example: Aggregate demand represents the total spending in an economy.

47.english_meaning: The demand for money needed to carry out day-to-day buying and selling of goods and services.
47.hindi_meaning: लेनदेन के लिए मुद्रा की मांग (रोजमर्रा के क्रय-विक्रय के लिए आवश्यक धन)
47.example: Transaction demand for money increases as national income goes up.

47.hindi_meaning: मौद्रिक प्राधिकारी (वह केंद्रीय संस्था जो देश में मुद्रा आपूर्ति और मौद्रिक नीति को नियंत्रित करती है)
47.example: The Reserve Bank of India acts as the monetary authority of the nation.

47.english_meaning: Bank deposits that can be withdrawn by the depositor without prior notice, usually through cheques.
47.hindi_meaning: मांग जमा (ऐसे बैंक खाते जिनका पैसा ग्राहक द्वारा मांगने पर या चेक के जरिए तुरंत निकाला जा सकता है)
47.example: Current and savings account balances are classified as demand deposits.

47.english_meaning: Bank deposits that have a fixed period to maturity and cannot be withdrawn immediately without penalty.
47.hindi_meaning: सावधि जमा / समय जमा (एक निश्चित अवधि के लिए बैंक में जमा धन, जैसे फिक्स डिपॉजिट)
47.example: Fixed deposits are common examples of time deposits in commercial banks.

47.hindi_meaning: नगण्य / न के बराबर (इतना कम कि ध्यान देने योग्य न हो)
47.example: The intrinsic value of the paper in a currency note is negligible.

47.hindi_meaning: व्यापारी बैंक / वाणिज्यिक बैंक (जनता से जमा स्वीकार करने और ऋण देने वाली वित्तीय संस्थाएं)
47.example: Commercial banks play a vital role in the credit creation process.

47.hindi_meaning: चलनी नोट / कागजी मुद्रा (सरकार या केंद्रीय बैंक द्वारा जारी किए गए नोट)

101.example: The government uses the Consumer Price Index to track changes in the cost of living.

101.english_meaning: Taxes levied by the government on the net income or profit made by corporations and private sector firms.
101.hindi_meaning: निगम कर (कंपनियों और निजी फर्मों द्वारा कमाए गए मुनाफे पर लगने वाला कर)
101.example: An increase in corporate tax can affect the expansion plans of private businesses.

101.english_meaning: Financing a government budget deficit by borrowing money from the central bank, which can increase money supply and inflation.
101.hindi_meaning: घाटे की वित्तव्यवस्था (केंद्रीय बैंक से उधार लेकर सरकारी बजट के घाटे को पूरा करना)
101.example: Excessive deficit financing often leads to higher inflation rates in a developing country.

101.english_meaning: The official reduction in the value of a country's domestic currency in relation to foreign currencies under a pegged exchange rate system.
101.hindi_meaning: अमूल्यन (तय विनिमय दरों के तहत सरकारी कार्रवाई द्वारा देश की मुद्रा के मूल्य में आधिकारिक कमी करना)
101.example: The government announced a devaluation of the currency to boost exports.

101.english_meaning: A situation where two parties each hold an item the other wants, making trade possible without money in a barter system.
101.hindi_meaning: आवश्यकताओं का दोहरा संयोग (वस्तु-विनिमय प्रणाली में वह स्थिति जब दोनों पक्षों के पास एक-दूसरे की जरूरत की चीजें हों)
101.example: Barter trade requires a double coincidence of wants, which can be very difficult to find.

101.english_meaning: Individuals, households, businesses, or institutions that make economic decisions regarding production, consumption, and allocation.
101.hindi_meaning: आर्थिक एजेंट (वे व्यक्ति या संस्थाएं जो आर्थिक निर्णय लेते हैं)
101.example: Consumers and producers are key economic agents in any market system.

101.english_meaning: The macroeconomic principle that, over a short period with constant prices, aggregate output is determined solely by total aggregate demand.
101.hindi_meaning: प्रभावी मांग का सिद्धांत (यह सिद्धांत जिसके अनुसार अल्पकाल में कुल उत्पादन केवल कुल मांग पर निर्भर करता है)
101.example: Keynesian economics heavily relies on the effective demand principle to explain employment levels.

101.english_meaning: The capacity and process of organizing, coordinating factors of production, and taking financial risks to run a business.
101.hindi_meaning: उद्यमिता (उत्पादन के दौरान संगठन, समन्वय और जोखिम उठाने का कार्य)
101.example: Successful entrepreneurship drives innovation and creates new jobs in the market.

101.english_meaning: Based on forecasts, planning, or expectations; the planned or intended value of an economic variable before it actually occurs.
101.hindi_meaning: पूर्व-नियोजित / प्रत्याशित (किसी आर्थिक चर का नियोजित या योजनाबद्ध मूल्य, वास्तविक होने से पहले)
101.example: Ex ante investment refers to the amount of investment that businesses plan to make.

101.english_meaning: Based on actual results or historical data; the realized or actual value of an economic variable after the event.
101.hindi_meaning: वास्तविक / पश्चातवर्ती (किसी आर्थिक चर का वास्तविक या प्राप्त मूल्य, घटना के बाद)
101.example: Ex post savings often equal ex post investment in macroeconomic accounting.

101.english_meaning: The component of an economy that deals with economic transactions, trade, and financial flows with the rest of the world.
101.hindi_meaning: बाह्य क्षेत्र (देश का वह क्षेत्र जो शेष विश्व के साथ होने वाले आर्थिक लेन-देन और व्यापार से संबंधित है)
101.example: Exports and imports form a major part of a country's external sector performance.

102.english_meaning: Benefits or harms accruing to a third party as a result of an economic activity without any compensation or payment.
102.hindi_meaning: बाह्य प्रभाव (वे लाभ या हानियां जो किसी आर्थिक गतिविधि के कारण किसी दूसरे व्यक्ति या संस्था को बिना भुगतान के प्राप्त होती हैं)
102.example: Factory pollution is a negative externality that harms the local community.

102.english_meaning: Government-issued currency that is not backed by a physical commodity like gold or silver and has no intrinsic value.
102.hindi_meaning: आदेशित मुद्रा (वह मुद्रा जिसका कोई आंतरिक मूल्य नहीं होता और यह सरकार के आदेश से चलती है)
102.example: Most modern paper currencies, such as the rupee or dollar, are fiat money.

102.english_meaning: Goods that are ready for consumption and do not undergo any further transformation in the production process.
102.hindi_meaning: अंतिम वस्तुएं (वे वस्तुएं जो उत्पादन प्रक्रिया में किसी और बदलाव से नहीं गुजरतीं और उपभोग के लिए तैयार होती हैं)
102.example: Bread purchased directly by a household is considered a final good.

102.english_meaning: The policy of a government regarding taxation, public spending, and borrowing to influence economic conditions.
102.hindi_meaning: राजकोषीय नीति (सरकार की वह नीति जो कर, सरकारी व्यय और ऋण से संबंधित होती है)
102.example: The government used expansionary fiscal policy to boost employment during the recession.

102.english_meaning: An exchange rate between currencies that is officially fixed at a certain level by the monetary authority and adjusted infrequently.
102.hindi_meaning: स्थिर विनिमय दर (वह विनिमय दर जिसे सरकार या केंद्रीय बैंक द्वारा निश्चित किया जाता है)
102.example: Under a fixed exchange rate system, the central bank maintains the currency's value at a pre-set level.

102.english_meaning: An exchange rate determined entirely by the market forces of supply and demand without central bank intervention.
102.hindi_meaning: लचीली विनिमय दर (वह विनिमय दर जो विदेशी मुद्रा बाजार में मांग और पूर्ति की शक्तियों द्वारा तय होती है)
102.example: A flexible exchange rate fluctuates daily based on market conditions.

102.english_meaning: Economic variables that are measured over a specific period of time.
102.hindi_meaning: प्रवाह (वे चर जिन्हें एक निश्चित समयावधि के दौरान मापा जाता है)
102.example: Income and monthly savings are examples of economic flows.

102.english_meaning: Foreign assets and currencies held by a country's central bank to back liabilities and influence monetary policy.
102.hindi_meaning: विदेशी मुद्रा भंडार (केंद्रीय बैंक द्वारा रखी जाने वाली विदेशी परिसंपत्तियां और मुद्राएं)
102.example: A healthy foreign exchange reserves level helps stabilize the domestic currency during economic shocks.

102.english_meaning: A measure of general price inflation calculated as the ratio of nominal GDP to real GDP.
102.hindi_meaning: जीडीपी अपस्फीतिकारक (नाममात्र जीडीपी और वास्तविक जीडीपी का अनुपात जो मूल्य स्तर में बदलाव को मापता है)
102.example: Economists use the GDP deflator to measure overall inflation within the domestic economy.

102.english_meaning: The numerical coefficient showing the magnified increase in total national output resulting from a unit increase in government spending.
102.hindi_meaning: सरकारी व्यय गुणक (वह संख्या जो दर्शाती है कि सरकारी खर्च में वृद्धि से कुल उत्पादन में कितना गुना बदलाव होता है)
102.example: An effective government expenditure multiplier can significantly stimulate a sluggish economy.

102.english_meaning: The severe worldwide economic depression that took place mostly during the 1930s, beginning with the 1929 stock market crash.
102.hindi_meaning: महामंदी (1930 के दशक का वह दौर जब दुनिया भर में उत्पादन में भारी गिरावट और बेरोजगारी में वृद्धि हुई थी)
102.example: The Great Depression caused widespread poverty and hardship across developed nations.

102.english_meaning: The total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.
102.hindi_meaning: सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (एक देश की घरेलू सीमा के भीतर उत्पादित सभी अंतिम वस्तुओं और सेवाओं का कुल मूल्य)
102.example: India's Gross Domestic Product grows steadily every year.

102.english_meaning: The excess of total government expenditure over revenue receipts and non-debt creating capital receipts.
102.hindi_meaning: सकल राजकोषीय घाटा (कुल सरकारी व्यय का राजस्व प्राप्तियों और गैर-ऋण पूंजीगत प्राप्तियों से अधिक होना)
102.example: Controlling the gross fiscal deficit is crucial for maintaining macroeconomic stability.

102.english_meaning: The total value of all goods and services produced by the residents and businesses of a country, regardless of production location, plus net factor income from abroad.
102.hindi_meaning: सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद (जीडीपी और विदेशों से शुद्ध साधन आय का योग)
102.example: Gross National Product includes income earned by citizens working overseas.

102.english_meaning: Money injected by the monetary authority (central bank), consisting mainly of currency in circulation and reserves held by commercial banks.
102.hindi_meaning: उच्च शक्ति प्राप्त मुद्रा (केंद्रीय बैंक द्वारा जारी की गई मुद्रा जो देश की मुद्रा आपूर्ति का आधार बनती है)
102.example: High powered money serves as the base for the creation of total money supply in the economy.

103.english_meaning: Goods that are used up during the process of production of other goods.
103.example: Milk used by a bakery to make biscuits is considered one of the intermediate goods.

103.english_meaning: The unsold goods, unused raw materials, or semi-finished goods carried from one year to the next.
103.example: The factory had to clear its old inventories before starting production for the new model.

103.english_meaning: The branch of economics that studies the economy as a whole, including inflation, growth, and national income.
103.example: John Maynard Keynes is widely regarded as the founder of modern macroeconomics.

103.english_meaning: Money issued by the government that legally cannot be refused by anyone for settling debts.
103.example: Currency notes issued by the central bank are recognized as legal tender throughout the country.

103.english_meaning: The function of a central bank in providing financial support to commercial banks facing liquidity crises.
103.example: During a financial panic, the Reserve Bank acts as the lender of last resort to prevent bank failures.

103.english_meaning: A situation of very low interest rates where people prefer holding cash rather than bonds, rendering monetary policy ineffective.
103.example: The economy struggled to recover as it fell into a deep liquidity trap with near-zero interest rates.

103.english_meaning: An exchange rate system where the central bank allows market forces to determine rates but intervenes when necessary.
103.example: To curb extreme volatility in the currency market, the central bank adopted a managed floating system.

103.english_meaning: The ratio of change in consumption to a change in total income.
103.example: An increase in household income often leads to a higher marginal propensity to consume.

103.english_meaning: The ratio of total money supply to the stock of high-powered money in an economy.
103.example: Commercial banks expand the money supply through the banking system, which determines the money multiplier.

103.english_meaning: Currency notes, coins, and demand deposits held by the public in commercial banks.
103.example: Narrow money represents the most liquid forms of money available in an economy.

103.english_meaning: Net National Product at market prices plus other current transfers from the rest of the world.
103.example: National disposable income gives a clearer picture of the total resources available to a nation's residents for consumption.

103.english_meaning: The aggregate value of goods and services produced domestically, excluding capital depreciation.
103.example: Net Domestic Product is calculated by subtracting depreciation from the Gross Domestic Product.

103.english_meaning: Addition to capital stock excluding the replacement for capital depletion.
103.example: Positive net investment indicates that the country's productive capacity is expanding.

103.english_meaning: The price of one country's currency in terms of another country's currency.
103.example: The nominal exchange rate tells you how many units of domestic currency are needed to buy one unit of foreign currency.

103.english_meaning: The reduction in the value of capital assets over time due to wear and tear.
103.example: Machinery undergoes depreciation every year as it is continuously used in production.

104.english_meaning: Gross Domestic Product evaluated at current market prices without adjusting for inflation.
104.hindi_meaning: मौद्रिक सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (चालू बाजार कीमतों पर मूल्यांकित जीडीपी)
104.example: Nominal GDP tends to rise when there is inflation in the economy.

104.english_meaning: The purchase or sale of government securities by the central bank to control the money supply.
104.hindi_meaning: खुले बाजार की क्रियाएँ (केंद्रीय बैंक द्वारा सरकारी प्रतिभूतियों की खरीद-बिक्री)
104.example: The central bank used open market operations to reduce money supply and curb inflation.

104.english_meaning: An economic theory suggesting that total savings may decrease when individuals try to save more during an economic downturn.
104.hindi_meaning: मितव्ययिता का विरोधाभास (जब लोग अधिक बचत करना चाहते हैं, तो कुल बचत कम हो जाती है)
104.example: During a recession, the paradox of thrift can lead to a further drop in overall economic demand.

104.english_meaning: The income available to households after deducting personal taxes and non-tax payments from personal income.
104.hindi_meaning: व्यक्तिगत प्रयोज्य आय (करों के भुगतान के बाद खर्च करने योग्य व्यक्तिगत आय)
104.example: An increase in personal disposable income usually leads to higher consumer spending.

104.english_meaning: A commodity or service that is collectively consumed, non-excludable, and non-rivalrous.
104.hindi_meaning: सार्वजनिक वस्तु (ऐसी वस्तु या सेवा जिसका उपयोग सभी के लिए सुलभ हो)
104.example: Street lighting is a classic example of a public good.

104.english_meaning: A theory of international exchange stating that the price of identical goods in different countries should be equalized when expressed in a common currency.
104.hindi_meaning: क्रय शक्ति समता (विभिन्न देशों में समान वस्तुओं की कीमतों का सिद्धांत)
104.example: Economists use purchasing power parity to compare the real cost of living across countries.

104.english_meaning: Gross Domestic Product evaluated at a set of constant prices, adjusted for inflation.
104.hindi_meaning: वास्तविक सकल घरेलू उत्पाद (स्थिर कीमतों पर मूल्यांकित जीडीपी)
104.example: Real GDP is a better indicator of economic growth than nominal GDP because it removes inflation effects.

104.english_meaning: The fraction of total deposits that commercial banks keep as reserves rather than lending out.
104.hindi_meaning: आरक्षित जमा अनुपात (वाणिज्यिक बैंकों द्वारा कुल जमा का आरक्षित रखा जाने वाला हिस्सा)
104.example: The central bank raised the reserve deposit ratio to restrict credit creation by commercial banks.

104.english_meaning: An official increase in the value of a country's currency within a fixed exchange rate system.
104.hindi_meaning: मूल्य पुनर्मूल्यांकन (नियत विनिमय दर प्रणाली में घरेलू मुद्रा का मूल्य बढ़ाना)
104.example: The government announced a revaluation of its currency to make foreign imports cheaper.

104.english_meaning: The excess of government revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
104.hindi_meaning: राजस्व घाटा (जब सरकार का राजस्व व्यय उसकी राजस्व प्राप्तियों से अधिक हो जाता है)
104.example: A high revenue deficit indicates that the government is borrowing for its day-to-day expenses.

104.english_meaning: An economic hypothesis that government debt financing does not affect overall consumer demand because people anticipate future taxes.
104.hindi_meaning: रिकार्डियन समतुल्यता (सिद्धांत जिसके अनुसार सरकारी ऋण भविष्य के करों की आशंका के कारण उपभोग को प्रभावित नहीं करता)
104.example: Ricardian equivalence suggests that tax cuts funded by debt will not stimulate the economy.

104.english_meaning: The demand for holding money as a store of wealth or to take advantage of future investment opportunities.
104.hindi_meaning: सट्टेबाजी के लिए मुद्रा की मांग (धन के संचय या निवेश लाभ के लिए पैसे की मांग)
104.example: Interest rates heavily influence the speculative demand for money.

104.english_meaning: The fraction of deposits that commercial banks must maintain in specified liquid assets as mandated by the central bank.
104.hindi_meaning: वैधानिक तरलता अनुपात (एसएलआर - बैंकों द्वारा तरल संपत्तियों के रूप में रखा जाने वाला अनिवार्य हिस्सा)
104.example: Commercial banks must maintain a specific Statutory Liquidity Ratio prescribed by the RBI.

104.english_meaning: Monetary policy actions taken by a central bank to offset the effects of foreign exchange inflows on domestic money supply.
104.hindi_meaning: नसबंदी या स्टरिलाइजेशन (विदेशी मुद्रा प्रवाह के घरेलू मुद्रा आपूर्ति पर प्रभाव को बेअसर करने की केंद्रीय बैंक की कार्रवाई)
104.example: The central bank performed sterilisation operations to neutralize the impact of massive foreign investment inflows.

104.english_meaning: Economic variables that are measured at a specific point in time.
104.hindi_meaning: स्टॉक (वे चर जिन्हें समय के एक विशेष बिंदु पर मापा जाता है)
104.example: Wealth and capital are classic examples of economic stocks, unlike flows which are measured over a period.

105.english_meaning: The function of money that allows wealth to be saved and stored for future use.
105.hindi_meaning: मूल्य का संचय - भविष्य में उपयोग के लिए धन के रूप में धन को बचाकर रखना।
105.example: Gold and money often act as a store of value during economic uncertainty.

105.english_meaning: The demand for holding money in order to carry out everyday business transactions.
105.hindi_meaning: लेन-देन मांग - दैनिक लेन-देन करने के लिए मुद्रा की मांग।
105.example: People keep cash in their pockets to satisfy their daily transaction demand.

105.english_meaning: Payments made by the government or firms without receiving any goods or services in return.
105.hindi_meaning: हस्तांतरण भुगतान - सरकार या फर्मों द्वारा बिना किसी सेवा या वस्तु के बदले दिए जाने वाले भुगतान (जैसे पेंशन, छात्रवृत्ति)।
105.example: Government pensions and scholarships are classic examples of transfer payments.

105.english_meaning: The portion of a firm's profits that is not distributed among the factors of production as dividends or wages.
105.hindi_meaning: अवितरित लाभ - फर्मों द्वारा कमाया गया वह लाभ जिसे उत्पादन के कारकों में बांटा नहीं जाता है।
105.example: The company used its undistributed profits to fund the new factory expansion.

105.english_meaning: The percentage of people actively looking for jobs who are unable to find work.
105.hindi_meaning: बेरोजगारी दर - नौकरी न पाने वाले लोगों का कुल नौकरी की तलाश कर रहे लोगों से अनुपात।
105.example: The government aims to reduce the unemployment rate through new skill development schemes.

105.english_meaning: The role of money as a standard numerical unit for measuring and comparing the values of different goods and services.
105.hindi_meaning: हिसाब की इकाई - विभिन्न वस्तुओं के मूल्यों को मापने और तुलना करने के लिए मुद्रा की भूमिका।
105.example: Money serves as a common unit of account in modern market economies.

105.english_meaning: An unexpected variation in the stock of goods held by a firm due to unforeseen market changes.
105.hindi_meaning: मालसूची में अप्रत्याशित परिवर्तन - बाजार में अचानक बदलाव के कारण फर्म के स्टॉक में होने वाला अनियोजित बदलाव।
105.example: Weak sales led to an unplanned change in inventories for the retail store.

105.english_meaning: The net contribution made by a firm in production, calculated as the value of production minus intermediate goods used.
105.hindi_meaning: वर्धित मूल्य (मूल्य संवर्धन) - उत्पादन प्रक्रिया में किसी फर्म द्वारा किया गया शुद्ध योगदान।
105.example: Value added tax is levied on the enhancement of product value at each stage of production.

105.english_meaning: Financial compensation paid to workers for the services they render.
105.hindi_meaning: मजदूरी - श्रम द्वारा प्रदान की जाने वाली सेवाओं के बदले दिया जाने वाला भुगतान।
105.example: The daily wage of construction workers was increased last month.

105.english_meaning: An index that measures the changes in the average price of goods traded in bulk in wholesale markets.
105.hindi_meaning: थोक मूल्य सूचकांक - थोक में कारोबार होने वाली वस्तुओं की औसत कीमत में प्रतिशत परिवर्तन।
105.example: The Wholesale Price Index helps economists monitor inflation trends at the producer level.

105.english_meaning: An abundance of valuable possessions or money.
105.hindi_meaning: धन / संपदा - मूल्यवान संपत्ति या धन का भंडार।
105.example: The accumulation of wealth can be measured over a period of time.

105.english_meaning: A raw material or primary agricultural product that can be bought and sold.

116.hindi_meaning: गुणक (वह अनुपात जिससे निवेश में वृद्धि से आय में कई गुना वृद्धि होती है)
116.example: The investment multiplier shows how an initial change in spending affects the overall national income.

116.english_meaning: A system of parts working together in a machine or a process to achieve a particular result.
116.example: The multiplier mechanism explains the process of income generation in an economy.

116.english_meaning: A part or element of a larger whole, especially of a system or machine.
116.example: Tax revenue and government expenditure are key components of the government budget.

116.english_meaning: The action or process of classifying something according to shared qualities or characteristics.
116.example: The classification of receipts helps in understanding government finances clearly.

116.english_meaning: Amounts of money received, especially by a government or organization.
116.hindi_meaning: प्राप्तियाँ (सरकार को मिलने वाला कुल धन)
116.example: Government receipts include both tax and non-tax revenues.

116.english_meaning: The action of spending funds or an amount of money spent.
116.example: Capital expenditure creates long-term assets for the country.

116.english_meaning: An amount of something left over when requirements have been met; excess of revenues over expenses.
116.hindi_meaning: अतिरेक या बचत (आय का खर्च से अधिक होना)
116.example: A surplus budget occurs when government receipts exceed expenditures.

116.english_meaning: The amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small or short.
116.hindi_meaning: घाटा (खर्च का आय से अधिक होना)
116.example: Fiscal deficit is a major concern for developing economies.

116.english_meaning: The branch of economics concerned with large-scale or general economic factors, such as interest rates and national productivity.
116.example: Open economy macroeconomics deals with international trade and capital flows.

116.english_meaning: The action of paying someone or of being paid, or sums of money paid.
116.example: The balance of payments records all economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world.

116.english_meaning: Wealth in the form of money or other assets owned by a person or organization or contributed for a purpose.
116.example: The capital account records foreign investments and loans.

116.english_meaning: The process of calculating or establishing something exactly.
116.example: Market forces are responsible for the determination of the exchange rate.

116.english_meaning: The quality of being particularly good or worthy, especially so as to deserve praise or reward; advantages.
116.example: We must weigh the merits and demerits of a flexible exchange rate system.
Inflation is one of the major demerits of certain monetary policies.

116.english_meaning: Free to move or be moved about; not fixed in position (referring to exchange rates).
116.hindi_meaning: लचीला या तैरता हुआ (बाजार आधारित विनिमय दर)
116.example: Managed floating allows central banks to intervene in the foreign exchange market.
